prompt:
Do crunch's calc threads all behave the same, or is one of them different? How?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: yes

## Main difference

Across the whole trace (offsets **0–30,554.3 ms**), **calc-0 (TID 633757)** is the outlier. It ran for **12,107.9 ms**, versus **3,086.3 ms** for the median of the other calc threads—about four times as much CPU time.

Across **300 rounds**, calc-0 finished its work **40.501 ms** into a round on average. The other calc threads’ last finisher averaged **10.600 ms**, so calc-0 finished about **29.902 ms later**. This is identified as a **significant hold-up** for crunch: its rounds would be about **73.8% shorter** if calc-0 kept up with the others.

## What explains it

The main thread, crunch (TID 633755), waited on calc-0 for **100% of its waits on other threads**—**300 waits totaling 12,134.0 ms**. In that wait chain, calc-0 was doing its own CPU work, averaging **40.352 ms per wait**.

One typical example occurred at offset **27,600.6 ms**: crunch’s **40.551 ms** wait depended on calc-0 running for that same **40.551 ms**.

The pattern is consistent across rounds: the median delay was **40.601 ms** (p99 **41.637 ms**), rather than being an occasional spike. TMLL’s syscall table reports **599 futex calls** for calc-0 totaling **17,807.2 ms**, but **zero futex wait time** there; the wait-chain analysis attributes the recurring hold-up to calc-0’s running work.

## The other calc threads

The remaining seven calc threads are much alike: each ran for about **3,082–3,129 ms** total (roughly **10.3–10.4%** of its time) and finished around **10.4–10.6 ms** into a round on average. They spent about **89.4–89.6%** of their time blocked. So the difference is principally **calc-0 doing substantially more work and finishing much later**, not one of the other seven behaving differently.
